identification: Boxed Hornby Railways (Australian range) electric train set: VR blue and gold diesel with three VR blue passenger cars, consistent with the Spirit of Progress set (R.572 in 1976, R.773 in 1977-78 per hornbyguide.com, with a VR B class diesel and passenger, dining and baggage cars); the set number is not visible in any photo. Plus a boxed Bachmann 'The Yard Boss' N scale set (tray shows tank car, boxcar, flat car, caboose, track and power pack; no locomotive visible), and a tray of Hornby extras: boxed Operating Royal Mail Coach, loose mail coach, controller/transformer, tunnel portal, station buildings, track and trees

viewing_check: Read the set number on the Hornby box ends or lid (R.572 or R.773 if it is the Spirit of Progress set). The box in the photos looks different from the R773 box that sold for A$324 (that one had a 'Spirit of Progress set' label and a boy photo; hornbyguide.com says the box style changed in 1978), and the right-hand compartment holds green and grey wagons that are not part of that set, so check what is original. The A$324.30 R773 sale includes a A$19.02 buyer protection fee (about A$305 to the seller), 2 bids. Check the diesel runs and the coaches have couplings. No Australian-located Yard Boss sale in the last 90 days; US sales run about A$65-180 and US postage alone is about A$84. Carters lists a sale of three Hornby sets including an R.773, but the price is behind a subscriber login.
